V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generator endomorphisms satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y, and xy-yx=h.

output.statement: e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. On the basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

argument.text: H001 gives n>0 and the finite index set I. From H002 and H003, induction on t gives hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v and, for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Indeed h y=y h-2y gives the h step. For x, the base is xyv=yxv+hv=λv; if xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v, then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ-t+1)+λ-2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ-t)y^t v. The t=0 h identity is hv=λv. Iterating the x identity, for 0≤i≤λ, gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v≠0: every factor is a positive integer when i>0, and the empty product is 1 when i=0. Thus e_i≠0 for every i∈I.

produces.statement: For every s≥0, hy^s v=(λ-2s)y^s v, and for s≥1, xy^s v=s(λ-s+1)y^{s-1}v. Every e_i for i∈I is nonzero.

argument.text: Take arbitrary c:I→C and temporarily assume L1: ∑_{i∈I} c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). F001 makes every summand except the j-th vanish, leaving c_j ∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. Its vector and scalar factors are nonzero over C, so c_j=0. Discharge L1; the family e is linearly independent. H002 gives dim_C V=n=card(I), so M003 makes its span all of V. Independence and spanning are precisely the basis conditions. The h formula at t=λ+1 has eigenvalue -λ-2. Expanding y^{λ+1}v in this basis and comparing coefficients in h gives [-λ-2-(λ-2i)] times its i-th coefficient equal to zero. These multipliers are nonzero for all i∈I, hence y^{λ+1}v=0. Further powers vanish by applying y.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V, and y^{λ+1}v and every higher y-power on v vanish.

argument.text: Divide the identities in F001 by i! and use F002 to obtain xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For any r≥0, iterate these formulas r times and divide by r!: for r≤i the x coefficient is (λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!=binom(λ-i+r,r), and for i+r≤λ the y coefficient is (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). Outside those ranges the string has already hit zero, so the result is zero. The product ratios equal the integer binomial coefficients defined in D015: for natural A≥r, count ordered lists of r distinct elements of {1,...,A}. There are A(A-1)⋯(A-r+1) such lists, and each r-element subset occurs r! times, once per ordering. Hence binom(A,r)=A(A-1)⋯(A-r+1)/r!, also for r=0 by empty products. Substituting A=λ-i+r or A=i+r gives the displayed identities and integrality. At r=0 both products equal 1. This proves the full characteristic-zero coordinate statement.
